task: Polish: two-column-form drop-downs whose choices were cut at laptop widths (row-cards report, 'Still weakest' item 3)
errors: First --write pass used a sibling-based 'repeated row' heuristic that also matched cards with two .fields blocks, so most pages were silently skipped; caught by re-measuring (74 -> 14 instead of -> 4), replaced with the rows-reserve empty-host definition.
Stashed the venture changes and then ran the dist patch script, which read block-less sources; reverted dist with an unpatch script before taking 'before' screenshots.

CI changed-ventures/page-integrity caught two real faults: applyBlock inserted before a '</style></head>' line on patreon-fee-calculator (stray </style>; fixed: insert at </head> when it shares a line, with a test), and the report lacked doc_index front matter (added).

doc_friction.issue: Item 3 guessed the other bid calculators shared the row-table layout; a select-clip run showed their cut selects are in the main two-column .fields grid instead, a different fix.
Measures only the default option; a tool that decides layout has to measure every option, so select-span re-implements the measure rather than reusing it.
Report front matter (`kind`) is required by doc_index.py, which no pull-request check names until changed-ventures runs it; copying an earlier report's header would have avoided it.

deviations.why: Did not screenshot the hub, a research page, Stories and a blog post before picking; the previous polish run's report named a measured next item and select-clip quantified it (74 cut on 47 pages).
deviations.did: Picked from the report and measured before and after on the built site.

certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured
